clue.text: And pressed for revolutionary music perhaps

definitions.text: And pressed for revolutionary music perhaps

parts.words: And pressed for revolutionary music perhaps
parts.note: a gramophone disc is pressed with a spiral cut, and turns round and round on the turntable to give its music

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into backing a revolution in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests politics, but here a record revolves on a turntable; the disc is pressed from a master that has a spiral channel cut into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that has been pressed carries the spiral track that holds its music.

parts.note: the region of Egypt given to Jacob and his family in the Book of Genesis

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the land in Egypt where Jacob's family settled bears this name.

clue.text: Manages, in division, to be called a this

definitions.text: Manages, in division, to be called a this

parts.words: Manages, in division, to be called a this
parts.note: split the word manages into two and it reads man ages, and an ageing man earns this name

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a department earns a certain title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In division' tells you to split 'Manages' into MAN AGES: a man who ages comes to be called an elderly person.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person, someone getting on in years, is called this.

clue.text: Namely expansion of Devizes town centre

definitions.meaning: that is to say, introducing a list
the middle three letters of Devizes are V, I and Z, the short form of the Latin word in full

explanation.surface: The plan to expand the centre of the Wiltshire town of Devizes.
explanation.walkthrough: Devizes is a market town in Wiltshire; its middle letters spell VIZ, and the full Latin word that VIZ abbreviates is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word, usually shortened to viz, means that is to say.

clue.text: Richer round cheese ? Don't you understand ?

definitions.meaning: a double version of a round cheese from Holland would be richer

explanation.surface: A diner is puzzled by an extra-rich wheel of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is incomprehensible is called this, and a doubled Holland cheese would be twice as rich.

clue.text: Directions to Scone perhaps, but not Bannockburn

definitions.text: Directions to Scone perhaps, but not Bannockburn

parts.words: Directions to Scone perhaps, but not Bannockburn
parts.note: the instructions for baking a scone, read as a route to the Scottish town of Scone, while nearby Bannockburn is a battlefield and no bannock bake

explanation.surface: Road directions to one Scottish town, but not to its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Scone and Bannockburn are places in Scotland near Stirling and Perth; a scone and a bannock are also both baked goods, so 'directions' turns from a route into cooking instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery instructions for a dish, such as how to bake a scone, are what a cookbook prints.

definitions.meaning: an Ethiopian title for a prince or chief
Royal Academicians, painters and sculptors with RA after their names

explanation.surface: A royal who leads the painters.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ethiopian ruler is called this, and Royal Academicians are RAs.

clue.text: He knows the price of everything and the value, of nothing (Wilde)

definitions.text: He knows the price of everything and the value, of nothing (Wilde)

parts.words: He knows the price of everything and the value, of nothing (Wilde)
parts.note: Oscar Wilde's definition, from Lady Windermere's Fan, of a sneering doubter of others' motives

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde's famous line about a person who values nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's line in Lady Windermere's Fan describes a sneering doubter who distrusts all motives.

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: to spoil something is to wreck it, so the letters of cane are jumbled

explanation.surface: A father ruins a cane, a remedy for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' reworks CANE into NACE, which sits between PA and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A universal remedy, a supposed cure for every ill.

parts.note: anxious waiting, read as the state of being hung up, as in suspending something

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner waits for the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: The anxious waiting sense is also the state of being hung or suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious uncertainty while waiting, and also the state of hanging from something.

parts.note: a military band's snare instruments are slung at the player's side and struck loudly

explanation.surface: An army is soundly defeated on its flank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten on the flank' reads as a battle lost on one wing; really it is percussion carried at the hip and struck with sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Snare drums in a marching band hang at the player's side and are struck with sticks.

indicators.note: the two pole letters get the word for one placed between them, as if receiving it

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles, so something polarised sits between them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Back in the old days, someone became polarised.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman calendar's nones fell on the 7th or 9th day of the month, and in the church it is the office said at the ninth hour.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar this was a fixed date in each month, and in church usage a canonical hour.

clue.text: Turn of Lot 10, of oriental character ; praise it

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient
X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: a turn of something sends it round the other way, so the word lot is read backwards

explanation.surface: An auction lot, number ten, with an oriental look, gets a good word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of' reverses LOT to give TOL, which goes at the end after E (east) and X (ten); 'of character' and 'it' are padding of this old-style clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud something is to speak highly of it, a synonym of praise.

clue.text: For vitality, pedal from start to finish

parts.note: life means vitality or liveliness
to cycle is to pedal a bicycle

explanation.surface: To keep fit, a cyclist pedals the whole route from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole course of a living thing's existence, from birth through to death, which the phrase 'from start to finish' captures.
explanation.definitionFit: The series of stages an organism passes through from birth to death covers its whole existence.

parts.note: a duck's beak is called its bill, and stuffing it would meet any need

explanation.surface: Enough food to content the hungriest duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means meet the requirement; a duck's beak is its bill, so filling it would satisfy the greedy bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be just what is needed, and a duck's beak is called a bill.

parts.note: animals went into Noah's Ark two by two, in a line of pairs, and one such reptile is famous for weeping insincerely

explanation.surface: The animals boarding Noah's Ark look sad.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a crocodile is also a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, like the animals entering the Ark two by two; crocodiles were said to weep while eating their prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere weeping is named after the reptile once thought to shed tears while devouring its victims.

clue.text: A vessel with more than one captain no doubt

definitions.text: A vessel with more than one captain no doubt

parts.words: A vessel with more than one captain no doubt
parts.note: a ship carrying soldiers would have many army captains aboard as well as its master

explanation.surface: A ship with too many people in command.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship carries one captain, but one carrying soldiers carries many army captains too.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that transports soldiers carries many army officers of that rank.

clue.text: The case for carrying an offensive weapon

definitions.text: The case for carrying an offensive weapon

parts.words: The case for carrying an offensive weapon
parts.note: reads as a legal argument for being armed, but means the sheath holding a sword

explanation.surface: A legal argument in favour of going about armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a courtroom argument; it is a sheath, and the offensive weapon is a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath for a sword or dagger is a case in which the blade is carried.

clue.text: Healthy exercise for the body politic

definitions.meaning: a walk taken for the good of one's health
relating to the fundamental laws of a state

explanation.surface: A good walk would do the whole nation good.
explanation.definitionFit: A brisk walk for one's health has long been called by this name, and the same word describes a state's founding law.

parts.note: near means mean, like Dickens's miser Scrooge, and the closest relatives are next of kin

explanation.surface: Which relative is the stingiest?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old British word for stingy, like Dickens's miser Scrooge; it also gives the phrase for closest relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is old slang for stingy, so the superlative means meanest; it also describes the closest relatives.

clue.text: There's such confusion in articles of floral growth

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits inside the articles

parts.note: an and a are the two indefinite articles

indicators.note: confusion means disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddle among the items of a flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusion' turns SUCH into CHUS, which goes 'in' between AN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchusa, or alkanet, is a blue-flowered plant of the borage family.

definitions.meaning: a symptom of a head cold
as in not to be sniffed at; to do this at something is to scorn it

explanation.surface: A frosty sneering disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chill brings on this sudden expulsion of breath, and something not to be scorned is 'not to be sneezed at'.

parts.note: something a walker wears on the foot, read as a device that slows a wheel

explanation.surface: Something that slows a pedestrian down.
explanation.walkthrough: A walker wears footwear, and the block pressed against a wheel to slow it is named after that footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The block that presses on a wheel to slow it is a braking part shaped like footwear.

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A traffic jam in a road network.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run not scored off the bat, such as a bye or wide, is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run added to the score but not hit by the batsman.

indicators.note: the letters for heated are to be taken out of the words before

parts.note: taken as written
something heated is hot

explanation.surface: Hope cannot remove a heated nut.
explanation.walkthrough: Take H and O from the start of HOPECANT and T from its end, in that order, leaving PECAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a well-known edible kernel from a hickory tree of the southern United States.

clue.text: Return thanks about the padre but keep from coming

indicators.note: returning something sends it back, so the whole assembly is read the other way
the word for thanks goes round the clergyman's title

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks
Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a padre or priest

explanation.surface: A thank-you is returned to the padre, but he is asked not to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps TA round REV to give TREVA, and 'Return' then reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off or prevent a danger is to stop it happening.

clue.text: Domestic life on the ocean wave in Yorks ?

definitions.text: Domestic life on the ocean wave in Yorks

parts.words: Domestic life on the ocean wave in Yorks
parts.note: a home on a two-masted sailing ship, read as the name of a Yorkshire town

explanation.surface: Living at sea, with a Yorkshire connection.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighouse is a town in West Yorkshire; a brig is a two-masted sailing ship, so a 'brig house' is a home at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The West Yorkshire mill town's name splits into a sailing ship and a dwelling.

definitions.meaning: an alcove or projecting window space

explanation.definitionFit: The laurel tree has this name, and so does an alcove or window recess.

definitions.note: adjective in the clue, standing for a noun naming a herb

indicators.note: the article goes inside the word for song

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece in a song about herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Dittany is an aromatic plant used in folk medicine and cookery, so it belongs among herbs.

parts.note: the French definite article la, as the clue's 'in France' signals
to place something is to locate it

explanation.surface: A star-gazer settled himself firmly in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre-Simon Laplace was a French mathematician and astronomer; 'in France' says the definite article is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Simon Laplace was the French scientist who wrote on celestial mechanics.
